title: Protecting Your Bones
hook: Bone looks permanent, but it's living tissue that thins with age. Osteoporosis weakens it silently until a minor fall causes a major break.
key_points: Bone density peaks in early adulthood, then gradually declines — faster after menopause.
Osteoporosis makes bones fragile and often has no symptoms until a fracture occurs.
Weight-bearing and strength exercise, plus enough calcium and vitamin D, help maintain bone.
Bone-density screening is recommended for older adults, especially women.
content_html: We picture bones as the body's permanent scaffolding, but they're living tissue, constantly broken down and rebuilt. With age the balance tips toward loss — and that quiet thinning is what makes a stumble dangerous later in life.
extra_html: The National Institute on Aging explains that bone density peaks in early adulthood and then slowly declines, with the loss accelerating for women after menopause as estrogen drops. Osteoporosis — porous, fragile bone — typically develops without any symptoms, which is why the first sign is often a fracture from a fall or even a minor strain, commonly in the hip, spine, or wrist. The protective habits are familiar ones: weight-bearing activities like walking and strength training signal bone to stay dense, while adequate calcium and vitamin D supply the raw materials. The NIA also notes that bone-density screening (a DEXA scan) is recommended for older adults — especially postmenopausal women — so that thinning bone can be caught and treated before it breaks.

related.title: Staying Strong as You Age
related.hook: The decline we associate with old age is partly the result of doing less. Staying active — in four distinct ways — keeps you independent far longer.

related.title: Why Strength Training Matters
related.hook: Cardio gets the glory, but lifting, resistance bands, and bodyweight moves protect something running can't: the muscle and bone you'll rely on for decades.

related.title: Do Calcium and Vitamin D Pills Really Protect Bones?
related.hook: Calcium and vitamin D pills are almost automatic for aging bones. But a review of nearly 154,000 people found that for most older adults, they barely move the needle on fractures or falls.

flashcards.prompt: Why is osteoporosis often called a 'silent' disease?
flashcards.back_html: It usually causes no symptoms as bone thins — many people don't know they have it until a minor bump or fall causes a fracture.

flashcards.prompt: Which combination helps maintain bone strength?

choices.text: Weight-bearing exercise plus enough calcium and vitamin D

flashcards.explanation_html: The NIA notes that weight-bearing and muscle-strengthening exercise, along with adequate calcium and vitamin D, help build and preserve bone.
